name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district lean (D+6 PVI) plus a favorable national environment
Incumbent Bill Keating running with a large cash advantage ($512K vs $52K)

model.rationale: Keating combines incumbency, a big fundraising edge, and a district that leans Democratic in an environment favorable to the party, while markets price his reelection at 97%. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or an unexpected outside-spending surge for MacAllister would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Keating seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by six points on the partisan baseline. He enters the general election with about $512,000 on hand, roughly ten times the cash of Republican Tyler MacAllister, who has raised modestly and shows no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing.

Prediction markets put Keating's chances near 97%, and the favorable national environment adds to his edge. The expected outcome is a double-digit Democratic margin, with the usual caveat that thin polling data leaves somewhat wider uncertainty than in well-surveyed races.
